test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, is also known as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**UMEED Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which is popularly referred to as the **UMEED Act**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 8, 2024**.
 
• The acronym **UMEED** stands for **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development**. This name reflects the government's objective to modernize and streamline the administration of Waqf properties in **India**.
 
• The bill was introduced by **Kiren Rijiju**, the Union Minister of **Minority Affairs**, aiming to amend the existing **Waqf Act, 1995**, which had been criticized for lacking transparency and accountability.
 
• One of the primary **features** of the **UMEED Act** is the mandatory **registration** of all Waqf properties on a **centralized portal** to ensure better monitoring and prevent illegal encroachments.
 
• The act proposes significant changes to the composition of the **State Waqf Boards** and the **Central Waqf Council**, including the mandatory representation of **two women** and **two non-Muslim** members to ensure a more inclusive administrative structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context of Waqf Laws:**
 
 
• The first major legislation was the **Waqf Act, 1954**, which was later replaced by the more comprehensive **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• In **2013**, the **United Progressive Alliance (UPA)** government introduced amendments to provide more powers to the Waqf Boards, but the current **2024-2025** amendment seeks to balance these powers with **government oversight**.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Waqf:**
 
 
• **Waqf** refers to the permanent dedication of movable or immovable **property** for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
• The person making such a dedication is known as a **Wakif**, and the manager of the property is called a **Mutawalli**.
 
 
 
• **Central Waqf Council:**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** established in **1964** by the **Government of India** under the original Act.
 
• Its **function** is to advise the Union Government on matters concerning the working of **State Waqf Boards** and the due administration of Waqf properties in the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Waqf-al-Aulad:**
 
 
• This refers to a **Waqf** created for the maintenance and support of the donor's own **family** and descendants. The **UMEED Act** seeks to bring more clarity to the rights of women in such family-based endowments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the District Collector:** Under the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, the power to conduct a **survey** of Waqf properties and decide whether a property is "Waqf" or "Government land" has been transferred from the **Survey Commissioner** to the **District Collector**.
 
• **Removal of 'Waqf by User':** The new bill proposes to remove the concept of **Waqf by User**, meaning a property cannot be declared as Waqf merely because it has been used for religious purposes for a long **duration**; it now requires a formal **Waqfnama** (deed).
 
• **Financial Audits:** To increase **efficiency** and reduce corruption, the act mandates that the **accounts** of Waqf Boards be audited by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** of India or a designated authority.
 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):** Following intense debate in **Parliament**, the bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** consisting of **31 members** (21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha) for further scrutiny and stakeholder consultation.
 
• **Data and Scale:** India has the largest **landholding** under Waqf outside the Islamic world, with over **8.7 lakh** registered properties covering approximately **9.4 lakh acres** of land across various **states**.
